title: Veggie Supreme Pizza
subtitle: Roasted peppers, mushrooms, olives
description: Roasted peppers, mushrooms, olives. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Sauté watery vegetables
steps.instruction: Sauté mushrooms, peppers, and onion in olive oil over medium-high 10 minutes until moisture evaporates and edges brown. Wilt spinach 1 minute; squeeze dry. Wet veg on pizza = soggy Veggie Supreme.

steps.title: Preheat stone to 500°F
steps.instruction: Heat stone or steel at 500°F at least 40 minutes. Drain artichokes and quarter if large.

steps.title: Stretch, sauce, first cheese
steps.instruction: Stretch four 12–14 inch rounds. Sauce evenly; layer half the mozzarella. This anchors vegetables so they do not slide off at the peel.

steps.title: Load vegetables and top cheese
steps.instruction: Distribute sautéed veg, olives, and artichokes evenly. Top with remaining mozzarella and oregano. Veggie Supreme should look crowded but color still peeks through.

steps.title: Bake until center is fully set
steps.instruction: Bake 12–15 minutes until cheese browns at edges and the vegetable center is hot through. Loaded veg pies need the full time — pale cheese over wet veg means underbaked. Rotate once.

steps.title: Parmesan, rest, and cut
steps.instruction: Rest 3 minutes, sprinkle parmesan, cut 8 slices per pie. Fan on sheet trays for eight. No meat does not mean light eaters — keep a backup pie at 200°F on a rack.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Veggie Supreme Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Roasted peppers, mushrooms, olives. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.

adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free pizza crust.
